title: Decorator: wrap to add behaviour
summary: Cheese and HappyHour wrap anything with cost() and describe() and offer the same two methods, so they stack in any order. Each calls through, then adds its part. The base pizza is given.
code: # A wrapper keeps the interface of what it wraps, so wrappers stack in any order.
triggers: add optional features to an object at runtime, in any combination, without a subclass per combination
wrappers that keep the same interface: logging, caching, retries, add-ons
prompts: An HTTP client needs optional retries, request logging and auth headers. Teams combine them differently, and nobody wants a class for every combination.
A document exporter can add a header, a footer and page numbers in any combination the user ticks, and new options keep arriving.
invariant: Every wrapper offers the wrapped object's methods and calls through to it, adding its own part before or after.
mantra: Same interface in and out: call through, then add.
pitfalls: A wrapper that never calls the wrapped object replaces it instead of decorating it.
Order matters: HappyHour(Cheese(pizza)) discounts the cheese too; Cheese(HappyHour(pizza)) doesn't.
A subclass per combination (CheesePizza, CheeseHappyHourPizza, ...) explodes; wrap objects instead.
